source_title: How to Get a Capital Gain Statement for Mutual Fund schemes in India
text: You can get a capital gains statement from the registrars CAMS (camsonline.com) or KFintech (kfintech.com) using the PAN and email ID registered with your investments, or from each fund house's website. Capital gain statements are generally available after the financial year ends in March.
quote: Visit CAMS (https://www.camsonline.com) or KFintech (https://www.kfintech.com) Use your PAN and email ID registered with your investments Request a consolidated capital gains report (choose financial year, email delivery) Visit the website of each fund house you've invested in Use the PAN/email to generate your individual capital gain statement Some AMCs also allow consolidated download across their schemes Capital gain statements are generally available after financial year-end (March)
keywords: capital gains statement capital gain report tax statement itr how to get download cams kfintech

source_title: SEBI Circular - Product Labeling in Mutual Fund schemes: Risk-o-meter (SEBI/HO/IMD/DF3/CIR/P/2020/197)
organization: Securities and Exchange Board of India
text: A riskometer (Risk-o-meter) shows a mutual fund scheme's risk level. SEBI requires six levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High.
quote: Risk Level of a scheme will be depicted by "Risk-o-meter". Risk-o-meter shall have following six levels of risk for mutual fund schemes : i. Low Risk ii. Low to Moderate Risk iii. Moderate Risk iv. Moderately High Risk v. High Risk and vi. Very High Risk
